site.name: Office of the Cathedral Warden, Saint-Évrard-sur-Vère
site.concept: Civic-ecclesiastical office overseeing the fabric, hours, and public observances of the Cathedral of Saint-Évrard and its precinct.

card_pattern: Each module sits inside a tall pointed-arch silhouette with a thin ink-black stroke; a small gold-leaf quatrefoil is set into the spandrel at the top corner. Card titles use Fraunces small caps in cobalt; body copy in Source Sans 3, justified, with a generous 1.7 line-height. Two-line gold rules separate metadata (dates, hours) from descriptive prose; an inline fleur-de-lis terminates closing remarks.
design_rules: Vertical proportions dominate — narrow text columns, tall arched frames, oversized capitals. Ornament concentrates at structural transitions (page heads, section breaks, card corners) over a quiet parchment field tiled lightly with quatrefoils-in-square. Saturated cobalt and gold-leaf accents punctuate ink-black silhouettes; nothing pastel, nothing rounded — every arch is pointed.

pages.title: The Cathedral Warden — Saint-Évrard-sur-Vère
pages.content_brief: Landing page for the Office of the Cathedral Warden. A tall pointed-arch hero frames the Notre-Dame rose-window centerpiece beneath the wordmark and the line 'Ad fabricam custodiendam — for the keeping of the fabric.' Below, three arched modules summarise: today's offices and bell schedule, current works on the south transept, and the next public assembly of the Chapter. A foot-rule of oak-leaf ornament leads into a brief from Warden Aliénor de Charnay dated this Michaelmas.

pages.title: Hours, Offices & Public Access — Cathedral of Saint-Évrard
pages.content_brief: Practical visitor and citizen information. Tabular hours for Lauds (06:15), Terce (09:00), Sext (12:00), None (15:00), Vespers (18:00), and Compline (20:30); separate columns for ferial, festal, and Lenten observance. Notes on cloister access (closed Mondays), the ambulatory works barrier, the lift in the north tower (out of service until Candlemas), and quiet-hour expectations. Address: 4 Place du Chapitre, Saint-Évrard-sur-Vère.

pages.title: Fabric & Works — Conservation of the South Transept
pages.content_brief: A civic accounting of ongoing conservation. Lead-glazier Joscelin Marot reports on the re-leading of the south rose (panels 7–14 returned to frame, 15–22 in workshop). Master-mason Perrine Aubry's notes on the buttress pinnacle replacement, with stone sourced from the Vère valley quarry at Belmont. A schedule of scaffolding through Eastertide and the projected costs to the Fabric Fund (£42,180 of £58,000 raised).

pages.title: The Chapter & Its Officers
pages.content_brief: Roster of the governing Chapter. Warden: Aliénor de Charnay (since 2019). Sub-Warden: Hugues Belmont. Treasurer of the Fabric: Marguerite Olivier. Master of the Choristers: Cn. Étienne Vasquez. Clerk of Works: Perrine Aubry. Each with a brief paragraph on responsibilities and term. Closes with the constitutional note that the Office answers jointly to the Bishop's See and to the Commune of Saint-Évrard under the Concordat of 1873.

pages.title: Assemblies, Petitions & Public Notice
pages.content_brief: How citizens engage the Office. The next open Chapter assembly: Thursday 14 November, 19:00, in the Salle du Chapitre. Standing items: the bell-tower access petition (third reading), the Place du Chapitre paving works, and the night-illumination ordinance. Instructions for lodging a written petition with the Clerk (deadline 14 days before assembly). Minutes of the previous assembly (10 October) available on application.

pages.title: The Fabric Fund — Giving & Patronage
pages.content_brief: An account of the Fabric Fund, established 1881, which sustains the cathedral's structural conservation independent of liturgical revenues. Current campaign: South Transept Glazing (closes Pentecost 2026). Named patronage tiers from Friend (£25) to Founder of a Quarry (£5,000, naming a single glass quarry in restored panel). Bequests handled by notary Cabinet Théron, 12 Rue des Lices. Fund accounts audited annually and posted at Michaelmas.
